**Subject:** Follow-up and next steps  

Hi Suzanne,  

Thanks again for the great call. Here’s a quick recap and what comes next:  

**Key Takeaways**  
- Goal: strengthen positioning in the specialized surgeon market using a targeted B2B approach and digital-first outreach.  
- Your team already has strong digital assets—we’ll refine the messaging to make the service feel *essential*, not optional.  
- The four-pillar framework (AI targeting, LinkedIn automation, CRM integration, and scaling optimization) ensures predictable lead flow and measurable ROI.  
- We guarantee 15 qualified surgeon opportunities within 90 days, with projected growth of $90K–$120K in new annual profit after six months.  

**Next Steps**  
- I’ll send the condensed proposal and slide deck for you and Bill to review.  
- Please share feedback or questions once he’s had a chance to evaluate budget and priorities.  
- Happy to meet with both of you to walk through the data or automation details.  

Would Wednesday at 1:30 PM or Thursday at 10:00 AM CT work for a quick follow-up?  

Appreciate your time, Suzanne—excited about what’s ahead.  

Warmly,  
**Bethany Gifford**  
Founder | New Era Intel  
[Contact info / meeting link]

Subject: Follow up and next steps on the specialized surgeon growth plan

Hi Suzanne,

Thank you again for the call. Here is a clear recap for you and Bill, plus the next steps I will take on my side.

Market positioning and opportunity  
• Goal: dominate the specialized surgeon market by using a focused B2B approach that reaches new employer markets and traditional surgeons who want flexible, innovative solutions.  
• Your digital presence is strong. With 89% of B2B buyers researching online before outreach, we can capitalize on that momentum.  
• The per-patient model gives surgeons flexibility and a pricing edge. General competitors run about 23% higher, which creates a natural advantage.  
• The market has shifted to digital-first research and LinkedIn outreach. Manual methods are slow and expensive by comparison.  
• Messaging needs to position the service as essential, not optional, so you are viewed as the only viable choice.

Four-pillar client acquisition framework  
1) Intelligence Foundation: 70+ AI data markers to pinpoint ideal surgeon profiles and eliminate guesswork.  
2) Automated LinkedIn Outreach: replaces manual work and multiplies qualified engagement while your team focuses on education.  
3) Proprietary CRM: unifies lead data, automates reporting, and flags inefficiencies in real time.  
4) Accelerated Conversion and Scaling: continuous message testing and targeting refinement to shorten cycles and protect every marketing dollar.

Performance guarantees and financial impact  
• Guarantee: 15 qualified surgeon opportunities in 90 days, with nurtured, high-intent leads.  
• Baseline projection: one new surgical client per month at roughly 15,000 dollars in new annual profit.  
• Six-month maturity target: about 30,000 dollars monthly profit after scale.  
• Six-month run rate: 90,000 to 120,000 dollars in new annual profit added, using conservative assumptions at the lowest pricing tier.  
• Cost of inaction estimate: about 8,000 dollars in lost opportunity.

Investment options and terms  
• Two models: equity-based with shared revenue, or a lower upfront fee with a higher revenue share. Both include all tech, CRM access, and full delivery of the four pillars.  
• Recommended term: one year, with a six-month performance review, and 90-day checkpoints for adjustments.  
• Quarterly business reviews every 90 days to assess results, pivot if needed, and scale what works.

Proposed timeline  
• Week 1: research and message refinement.  
• Weeks 2 to 3: system setup and outreach automation.  
• By Week 6: campaign live.  
• From Week 7 onward: daily analytics and continuous optimization.

Client readiness and next steps  
• You confirmed Bill will review the proposal and budget with esthetics as a key focus area.  
• I offered to brief Bill directly and bring my technical team for any deep dives on data, automation, or financial modeling.

Action items  
• Bethany: I will send the detailed conversation breakdown and the growth plan slide deck for you and Bill today. I am available by email, text, or call for clarifications and a technical walk-through.  
• Suzanne: please share the materials with Bill, gather feedback and questions, and send them back to me so we can address everything in one pass.

If helpful, I can hold time for a brief working session with you and Bill. I can do Wednesday, October 29 at 1:30 PM CT or Thursday, October 30 at 10:00 AM CT. If another time is better, I will make it work.

Appreciate you, Suzanne. Looking forward to helping you lead this category and make the most of the coming budget cycle.

Warmly,  
Bethany Gifford  
Founder, New Era Intel

write a follow up email to Suzanne about our call: Market Positioning and Business Opportunity
The main goal is to dominate the specialized surgeon market by leveraging a unique B2B approach that targets new employer markets and traditional surgeons seeking innovative solutions (02:10).

Bethany Gifford highlighted that 89% of B2B buyers conduct extensive digital research before vendor contact, emphasizing the need for a strong digital presence, which Suzanne’s team already has (03:42).
The service’s edge lies in its specialized per-patient model that offers surgeons flexibility and differentiation from general competitors, who typically have 23% higher rates, creating a pricing advantage (05:09).
Market forces push toward digital-first research and LinkedIn-based B2B outreach, making manual and traditional sales methods inefficient and costly (06:44).
Messaging currently risks positioning the service as optional rather than essential, so refining it to portray the product as the only viable option is critical for market leadership (06:44).
Four-Pillar Client Acquisition Framework
The client acquisition strategy relies on a structured four-pillar framework that builds efficiency and scale (07:40).

Pillar one, the Intelligence Foundation, uses over 70 AI-powered data markers to precisely identify ideal surgeon profiles, eliminating guesswork and improving targeting accuracy (07:48).
Pillar two, automated LinkedIn outreach, replaces manual efforts, freeing up time and multiplying engagement capacity while allowing focus on client education and qualification (09:05).
Pillar three integrates a proprietary CRM system that unifies all lead data, automates reporting, and flags inefficiencies in real time, enabling quick pivots and data-driven decisions (10:32).
Pillar four, accelerated conversion and scaling, continuously refines messaging and targeting to shorten sales cycles and maximize every marketing dollar, ensuring no spend is wasted (11:56).
Performance Guarantees and Financial Impact
The team guarantees 15 qualified sales opportunities with surgeons within 90 days, emphasizing quality over quantity with nurtured leads rather than cold contacts (12:55).

The baseline projection expects one new surgical client per month generating approximately $15,000 in new annual profit, with a six-month maturity target of $30,000 monthly profit after scaling (14:58).
Within six months, acquiring one surgeon monthly could add over $90,000 in new annual profit, with an optimistic scenario reaching $120,000, all based on conservative estimates and the lowest pricing tier (16:21).
Failure to act may result in an estimated $8,000 lost opportunity, underscoring the cost of inaction in a competitive market (16:50).
Bethany stressed the difference from generic marketing firms by offering a risk-free, guaranteed sales pipeline and tailored narratives that speak directly to the surgeon audience (17:47).
Investment Options and Contract Terms
Two payment structures were presented: an equity-based model with shared revenue and a lower upfront fee with higher revenue share, both negotiable to fit B2B realities (18:49).

Both options cover full implementation of the four-pillar framework, guarantee delivery, and include all technology tools and CRM access without extra charges (21:00).
Bethany recommends a one-year contract with a six-month performance evaluation window to allow adequate time for growth and adjustment, though commitment can be reevaluated every 90 days (21:34).
Regular quarterly business reviews every 90 days will assess effectiveness, pivot strategies, or scale efforts as needed, reinforcing a growth partnership mentality rather than a fixed vendor relationship (21:20).
The proposed timeline starts with research and messaging refinement in week one, system setup and outreach automation over weeks two to three, campaign launch by week six, and ongoing daily data analysis from week seven onward (22:50).
Client Readiness and Next Steps
Suzanne confirmed that the CEO, Bill, who has deep tech and startup experience, will review the proposal and budget for next year, with a focus on esthetics as a key specialty (26:30).

Suzanne noted recent increased marketing investment under Bill’s leadership and acknowledged the time needed to implement current strategies, suggesting the proposal will be evaluated in that context (28:25).
Bethany offered to engage directly with Bill to clarify details, provide technical deep-dives, and include her detail-oriented team to ensure comprehensive understanding and alignment (30:49).
Both parties agreed to continue communication via email and potential follow-up calls after Bill’s review, aiming to finalize decisions based on detailed ROI and operational fit (32:30).
